connections.note: Canonical Creation narrative
Humanity, land, divine formation, vocation; a distinct creation narrative, thematically related rather than the same account as Genesis 1:1–2:3
Disorder, curse, mortality, exile from created/garden order — interpretive thematic link: the fall read against the created order
Repeats image/likeness language in human genealogy
Renewed blessing, multiplication, image of God; dominion phrasing here is less direct than in Genesis 1
Sabbath command explicitly grounded in six-day creation and seventh-day rest
Sabbath sign explicitly echoes creation/rest
Human glory, dominion over creatures; major image/vocation parallel — the royal-combat historical reconstruction behind it is contested, no consensus implied
Heavens, celestial order, sun imagery
Creation by divine word; gathering waters
Creator and sea-combat imagery in this psalm; Genesis 1 itself does not describe combat — the combat imagery belongs to Psalm 74
Extended creation hymn: waters, heavens, land, creatures, provision
Divine ordering and sea/chaos imagery
Creation, sea boundaries, cosmic architecture
Wisdom present at creation; thematic link only — no grammatical or syntactical link between Proverbs 8 and Genesis 1:1 is asserted (proposed syntax link removed pending verification)
Creator sovereignty used in prophetic consolation
God as creator of heavens/earth and giver of breath

Exclusive divine creation and ordering; the Hebrew verb bārāʾ (H1254) occurs six times in this range (Isa 45:7 ×2, 45:8, 45:12, 45:18 ×2), verified against the repo's Original Language data via the Preview API 2026-11-11
Redemptive victory expressed with Rahab/sea combat imagery; the historical exodus (sea deliverance) reference and the creation inference are distinct
Reuses tōhû wābōhû (Jer 4:23) in de-creation imagery — the Hebrew phrase (tōhû H8414, bōhû H922) verified against the repo's Original Language data via the Preview API 2026-11-11
Christian rereading of beginning, divine Word, life, light
Creation/light vocabulary integrated with incarnation theology — weaker as an independent Genesis 1 connection; labelled thematic only
Christological creation and “image” language
Genesis seventh-day rest applied typologically to rest; the 'eschatological' reading is an interpretive application, attributed rather than asserted as the text's own claim
Creation from/through water and later judgment
Worship of God as creator
New heaven/new earth and removal of former disorder
Creation/Eden motifs: river, tree of life, light, human reign — mostly relates to Genesis 2–3 rather than Genesis 1
